scope: Corollary 9.1 (Tropical feasibility and fixed corank) of the manuscript “Deterministic quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games” (preprints/Deterministic-quasipolynomial-time-mean-payoff-games-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 104 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5d8d8876fd2982fd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For explicitly listed m × n matrices A, B and m-dimensional vectors c, d over Q ∪ {−∞}, feasibility of max   ci, max j (Aij + xj) ≤ max   di, max j (Bij + xj) for every row i is decidable deterministically in 2O((log(L+2))2) bit operations, where L is the complete explicit binary input length. Variables range over R ∪ {−∞}; feasibility with all coordinates finite is decidable within the same bound. Equalities between the two displayed maxima are allowed, interpreted as pairs of inequalities. For a homogeneous system (c = d = −∞), one can also compute the maximal finite-coordinate support of a solution, including the empty support. In particular, the same bound decides feasibility of max-atom systems z ≤ max(x, y) + a, with rational constants a and finite real, equivalently rational, variables. For each fixed integer k ≥ 0, a deterministic algorithm with bit bound 2Ok((log(L+2))2) decides whether an explicitly listed m × n matrix over Q ∪ {−∞}, with m ≥ n ≥ 1, has tropical rank at least n − k. Here tropical rank is the largest order of a square submatrix whose permutation sums have a finite, unique maximum. The rank is zero if no such nonempty submatrix exists.
